x: Article 368 states that Parliament may, in exercise of its constituent power, amend the Constitution by way of addition, variation or repeal of any provision, subject to the basic-structure limitation.

s: Who described the constitutional amendment process as appearing 'complicated' but being 'merely diverse'?
x: Granville Austin said the process appears complicated but is merely diverse, calling it one of the most ably conceived aspects of the Constitution.

s: As of 2026, which is the latest constitutional amendment to have been enacted in India?
x: The 106th Amendment (2023) is the latest enacted amendment. The 101st (2016, GST) and 104th (2020) are earlier enactments, and the 131st was only a Bill that failed in the Lok Sabha in April 2026.

s: Which Article and Part of the Constitution govern the amendment powers and procedure?
x: Article 368, in Part XX, gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and sets the procedure. Article 356 is President's Rule and 280 the Finance Commission.

s: Which one of the following best characterises the nature of the Indian constitutional amendment procedure?
o: It is entirely flexible because every provision can be changed by ordinary law.
It is rigid only in matters relating to Fundamental Rights.
It is a synthesis of rigidity and flexibility.
It is entirely rigid because every provision requires State ratification.
x: The Indian Constitution combines different methods of amendment and is therefore neither purely rigid nor purely flexible; it is a synthesis of both.

s: Besides the 24th Amendment, which Amendment amended Article 368 itself?
x: Article 368 was amended by the 24th (1971) and the 101st (2016) Amendments.

s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal' and praised its balance between rigidity and flexibility?
x: K.C. Wheare called the Constitution quasi-federal and saw a good balance of rigidity and flexibility in its amendment procedure.

s: By which Amendment was Article 13(4) inserted?
x: The 24th Amendment inserted Article 13(4), clarified Parliament's power to amend FRs and made presidential assent to amendment Bills obligatory.

s: What does the Constitution provide in case of a deadlock between the two Houses over an Ordinary Bill?
o: Passage by the Lok Sabha alone
A final decision by the President
x: An ordinary Bill needs a simple majority, both Houses have equal powers over it, and a deadlock can go to a joint sitting.

s: In which manner may a Bill for amendment of the Constitution be introduced?
o: By a minister or a private member, without the President's prior permission
Only by a minister, with the President's prior permission
Only after ratification by the States
x: An amendment Bill needs no prior presidential permission and may be moved by a private member; Article 108 joint sittings do not apply to it.

s: By which Amendment was it made obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill?
x: The 24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 made the President's assent to a constitutional amendment bill obligatory.

s: Which type of Bill may require ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures?
o: Constitution Amendment Bill affecting federal provisions
x: Constitution Amendment Bills affecting specified federal provisions need ratification by at least half the States; ordinary Bills need only a simple majority in Parliament.

s: Where must a Constitution Amendment Bill be passed by a special majority?
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
The Lok Sabha, with recommendations from the Rajya Sabha
x: An amendment Bill can start in either House without the President's recommendation and needs a special majority in each House separately; there is no joint sitting.

s: What does a special majority for amending the Constitution mean?
o: Three-fourths of the members present and voting in each House
Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
A majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of members present and voting
A majority of members present and voting in a joint sitting
x: Special majority combines two requirements in each House: a majority of the total membership and a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

s: By what majority does a State Legislature ratify a Constitution Amendment Bill?
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
Majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting
x: Ratification is by a simple majority of each concerned State Legislature, and no time limit is prescribed for it.

s: What can the President do once a Constitution Amendment Bill is duly passed?
o: May withhold assent in the public interest
May return it once for reconsideration
May refer it to a joint sitting
x: Assent to a duly passed amendment Bill is obligatory: the President can neither withhold it nor return the Bill (24th Amendment, 1971).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about presidential action on Bills?
o: The President may return a Money Bill once for reconsideration
The President may return an Ordinary Bill once
The President may withhold assent to an Ordinary Bill
The President may withhold assent to a Money Bill
x: A Money Bill can be assented to or withheld but never returned; only an ordinary Bill can be returned once.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the passage of Bills?
o: A Money Bill originates only in the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations
An Ordinary Bill may originate in either House, with equal powers for the Rajya Sabha
A Financial Bill (I) can only be recommended on, not rejected or amended, by the Rajya Sabha
A Constitution Amendment Bill may originate in either House and must pass each House separately
x: A Financial Bill (I) originates only in the Lok Sabha, but the Rajya Sabha has full power to reject or amend it.

s: What happens if either House of Parliament rejects a Constitution Amendment Bill?
o: A joint sitting is summoned to resolve it
x: There is no joint sitting for a Constitutional Amendment Bill, so rejection by either House causes failure; once duly passed, assent is obligatory under the 24th Amendment.

s: Which Article on joint sittings does NOT apply to Constitution Amendment Bills?
x: Article 108 (joint sitting) does not apply to amendment Bills, so each House must pass them separately.

s: How is a deadlock between the two Houses on a Constitution Amendment Bill resolved?
o: By a joint sitting under Article 108
There is no mechanism: a joint sitting is not available
By ratification of half the States
By reference to the Supreme Court
x: The Constitution provides no joint sitting for amendment Bills, so a deadlock cannot be resolved; this absence is itself a criticism of the procedure.

s: For which of the following is ratification by the States required?
o: Only a limited group of federal provisions
Only amendments passed by a joint sitting
x: State ratification is needed only for a limited group of federal provisions, not for every amendment.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a provision that may be amended by a simple majority outside Article 368?
o: The distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States
The number of puisne judges of the Supreme Court
x: The distribution of legislative powers, including the Seventh Schedule, is a federal provision requiring the prescribed State ratification. Citizenship, the Fifth and Sixth Schedules and the number of puisne judges of the Supreme Court are amendable by simple majority.

s: What time limit is prescribed for State ratification of an amendment affecting specified federal provisions?
x: State ratification is needed only for specified federal provisions, not every amendment, and no time limit is prescribed for it.

s: Amendments to specified federal provisions require ratification by how many State Legislatures?
o: At least one-half of the State Legislatures
x: Federal provisions need ratification by at least half the States; the President's qualifications and tenure need no ratification.

s: Which of the following requires a special majority of Parliament along with ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures?
x: The Seventh Schedule, the President's election and representation of States need State ratification; Fundamental Rights need only a special majority.

s: Which one of the following was added to the category of provisions requiring State ratification by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016?
x: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 added Article 279A relating to the GST Council to the federal provisions requiring State ratification.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Representation of States in Parliament – Article 11
Election of the President – Articles 54 and 55
x: Articles 54 and 55 concern the election of the President. The GST Council is Article 279A, State representation is the Fourth Schedule and citizenship is Article 11.

s: Which of the following statements about State ratification is incorrect?
o: The 3rd Amendment concerned Entry 33 of the Concurrent List.
Ratification requires a simple majority of at least one-half of the States.
Ratification by every State is mandatory.
The first amendment requiring State ratification was the 3rd Amendment of 1954.
x: Option C is incorrect: ratification needs only half the States, by simple majority in each, not all of them. The first amendment that needed it was the 3rd (1954), on Entry 33 of the Concurrent List.

s: The Supreme Court’s decision in Rajendra N. Shah (2021) is associated with which of the following?
o: Striking down Part IXB in its entirety for violating the federal structure without any further qualification
Invalidating the GST Council under Article 279A
Declaring the 24th Amendment unconstitutional for abridging Fundamental Rights
Striking down the provisions relating to State co-operative societies in Part IXB for want of ratification by the States
x: In Rajendra N. Shah (2021), the provisions of Part IXB relating to State co-operative societies were struck down for want of ratification by the required number of States.

s: Which of the following does NOT require ratification by the States?
x: The election of the President needs ratification, but his qualifications, conditions of office and tenure do not.

s: Representation of States in Parliament, an amendment to which needs State ratification, is contained in which Schedule of the Constitution?
x: Representation of States in Parliament (Rajya Sabha seats) is in the Fourth Schedule, a federal provision needing ratification by half the States.

s: By which procedure can Article 32 be amended?
o: A special majority plus ratification by half the States
A special majority of Parliament without State ratification
No procedure, as it cannot be amended at all
x: Article 32 may be amended by special majority without State ratification, though the Supreme Court's power under it is part of the basic structure.

s: Which of the following is required to amend the Directive Principles of State Policy?
o: Special majority plus ratification by half the States
x: DPSPs, like Fundamental Rights, are amended by special majority without State ratification.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 2 to Article 4 — Formation and alteration of States
Article 169 — Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils
x: Article 368 contains the general constitutional amendment procedure, whereas citizenship is among the matters that can be changed by simple majority under Article 11. Articles 2–4, 169 and 327 relate to the subjects stated.

s: Which one of the following subjects is amended by a simple majority of Parliament outside the procedure of Article 368?
x: Quorum is among the matters that can be altered by a simple majority outside Article 368. Fundamental Rights and DPSPs require the special majority procedure, while the election of the President also requires State ratification.

s: Which of the following is required to create or abolish a State Legislative Council under Article 169?
o: A simple majority of Parliament, outside Article 368
A special majority plus ratification by half of the States
A special majority of the State Legislature only
x: Legislative Councils are dealt with by simple majority outside Article 368; the President's election needs special majority plus State ratification.

s: How can changes relating to Articles 2, 3 and 169 of the Constitution be made?
o: A special majority plus ratification by half the States
A simple majority, without being deemed amendments under Article 368
x: Changes under Articles 2, 3 and 169 are made by simple majority and are not deemed amendments under Article 368; the Constitution has both flexible and rigid methods.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new States.
Article 4 provides that laws under Articles 2 and 3 are amendments under Article 368.
Article 3 deals with the formation of new States and alteration of boundaries.
x: B is incorrect: Article 4 says laws under Articles 2 and 3 are NOT amendments under Article 368 — they pass by simple majority. The others are right: Article 2 new States, Article 3 boundaries, Articles 5–11 citizenship.

s: An amendment Bill got 298 votes for and 230 against, with 528 present and voting. How many 'yes' votes did two-thirds need?
x: Two-thirds of 528 is 352; with only 298 votes in favour the Bill failed the two-thirds requirement.

s: What majority is required for the impeachment of the President of India?
o: Two-thirds of the total membership of the House concerned
Two-thirds of the members present and voting in both Houses
Majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting in both Houses
Three-fourths of the total membership of Parliament
x: Under the Article 61 type of majority, impeachment of the President requires two-thirds of the total membership of the House concerned.

s: The Article 368 type of special majority is relevant to which one of the following sets of provisions?
x: The Article 368 type of majority is used for removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges, the CAG, the CEC and State Election Commissioners, constitutional amendment, and approval of a National Emergency. The relevant provisions include Articles 124, 217, 148, 324, 243K and 352.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 368 type of majority – Legislation on a State List subject
Article 61 type of majority – Constitutional amendment
Article 312 – Creation of new All-India Services
x: Article 312 deals with creating new All-India Services. The Article 368 type majority is for constitutional amendment, the Article 61 type for impeaching the President, and Article 249 for legislating on a State List subject.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 61 – two-thirds of members present and voting in each House
Article 249 – two-thirds of total membership of the Lok Sabha
Article 312 – two-thirds present and voting in the Rajya Sabha only
Removal of the CAG – simple majority
x: Article 312 (new All-India Services) needs two-thirds present and voting in the Rajya Sabha; Article 61 needs two-thirds of total membership; CAG removal needs the Article 368 type.

s: Which of the following can NOT be changed by Parliament by a simple majority outside Article 368?
o: Formation of new States and alteration of their boundaries
Creation or abolition of Legislative Councils in States
The basic structure of the Constitution
Change in the official language under Article 343
x: The basic structure cannot be amended even by the special procedure; the other three are simple-majority matters outside Article 368.

s: Which case(s) held that constitutional amendments are not 'law' under Article 13(2)?
x: Shankari Prasad and Sajjan Singh held so; Golaknath barred abridging FRs, Kesavananda allowed amendment within the basic structure, and Minerva Mills held limited amending power basic.

s: What was the effect of the Constitution (24th Amendment) Act, 1971 on Articles 13 and 368?
o: It declared every constitutional amendment to be ordinary law under Article 13.
It empowered Parliament to amend Fundamental Rights and inserted Article 13(4), excluding an Article 368 amendment from the term ‘law’ in Article 13.
It prohibited Parliament from amending Fundamental Rights and removed Article 368.
It made all constitutional amendments subject to approval by a national referendum.
x: The 24th Amendment amended Articles 13 and 368, empowered Parliament to abridge or take away Fundamental Rights and inserted Article 13(4), under which an amendment made under Article 368 is not ‘law’ for Article 13.

s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the amending power of Parliament in chronological order:
A. Golaknath judgment
B. Shankari Prasad judgment
C. Kesavananda Bharati judgment
D. Twenty-Fourth Constitutional Amendment
x: The correct sequence is Shankari Prasad (1951), Golaknath (1967), the 24th Amendment (1971), and Kesavananda Bharati (1973).

s: The Kesavananda Bharati judgment upheld which Constitutional Amendment?
x: Kesavananda Bharati upheld the 24th Amendment and held that FRs and the Preamble are amendable but the basic structure cannot be altered.

s: Which case first applied the basic-structure doctrine?
x: Kesavananda Bharati first propounded the doctrine and Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain first applied it; Golaknath first limited the amending power over FRs.

s: Which Amendment inserted clauses (4) and (5) in Article 368 to bar judicial review of constitutional amendments?
x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 inserted Article 368(4) and (5) to declare the amending power unlimited and bar judicial review of amendments.

s: Which case held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights?
x: Golaknath held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights; Sajjan Singh had earlier upheld that power.

s: What did Kesavananda Bharati (1973) hold about Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights?
o: Parliament cannot amend them at all
Parliament can amend them only with State ratification
Parliament can amend them only by a joint sitting
Parliament can amend them but not destroy the basic structure
x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973, 13 judges) held that Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights but cannot destroy the Constitution's basic structure.

s:
Assertion (A): Minerva Mills invalidated clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368.
Reason (R): The case reaffirmed that a limited amending power is itself a Basic Feature.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true: Minerva Mills struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 (added by the 42nd Amendment) because a limited amending power is itself a basic feature. R explains A.

s: By what majority was the 13-Judge Bench in Kesavananda Bharati divided?
x: Kesavananda Bharati was decided by a 13-Judge Bench by a 7:6 majority.

s: On which date was the judgment in Kesavananda Bharati delivered?
x: The Kesavananda Bharati judgment was delivered on 24 April 1973.

s: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, which proposes a new Article 82A, relates to which of the following?
o: Simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
Reservation of one-third seats for women in the Lok Sabha
Increase in the strength of the Lok Sabha to 850
Removal of the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers on arrest
x: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024 concerns simultaneous elections and proposes a new Article 82A; it was referred to a Joint Committee. Women's reservation is the 106th Amendment (2023); raising Lok Sabha strength to 850 was the 131st Bill, 2026; removal of PM/CMs on arrest is a separate pending proposal.

s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposed raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to how many?
x: It sought 850 seats with delimitation but failed in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026 (298 for, short of the 352 needed); there is no joint sitting for amendment Bills.

s: India's amendment procedure has no special body (convention). Which of the following is it also without?
x: Critics note there is no special body or referendum for amendments; special majority, assent and State ratification all exist.

s:
Consider the following statements about criticism of the amendment procedure:
1. There is no time limit within which States must ratify an amendment.
2. State Legislatures may initiate amendments on federal provisions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is a recognised criticism. Statement 2 is wrong: States cannot initiate amendments at all.

s: What is the role of State Legislatures in amending the Constitution under Article 368?
o: They can initiate an amendment by resolution
They can introduce amendment Bills in Parliament on State subjects
They can refer amendment Bills to the Supreme Court
They can only ratify certain amendment Bills passed by Parliament
x: States cannot initiate amendments under Article 368; they only ratify amendments to specified federal provisions.

s: Which word in the Preamble was NOT added by the 42nd Amendment?
x: The 42nd Amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'; 'Justice' was already in the original Preamble.

s: Which of the following was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment?
x: The 42nd Amendment moved education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice to the Concurrent List.

s: When was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha?
x: The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in September 1976 during the Emergency period.

s: Which one of the following was a change made by the Forty-second Constitutional Amendment?
o: Extension of the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from five to six years
Abolition of tribunals under Part XIVA
Reduction of the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies to four years
Removal of Article 368 from the Constitution
x: The 42nd Amendment extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from five to six years. It also inserted Part XIVA relating to tribunals and froze delimitation on the basis of the 1971 Census.

s: Which Amendment enabled a National Emergency to be proclaimed in only a part of India?
x: The 42nd Amendment enabled Emergency in a part of India; it also inserted Part IVA (Fundamental Duties) and Part XIVA (tribunals).

s: Which Constitutional Amendment is known as the 'Mini-Constitution'?
x: The 42nd Amendment made sweeping changes, such as adding Fundamental Duties and 'Socialist, Secular and Integrity' to the Preamble.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the constitutional debate on secularism is correct?
o: The words ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment, while the Supreme Court has held that secularism is part of the basic structure.
The 103rd Amendment added both words to the Preamble.
The words ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ were added by the 44th Amendment and secularism is not a basic feature.
Both words were present in the original Preamble and have never been judicially examined.
x: The 42nd Amendment added the words ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ to the Preamble. The Supreme Court has also held that secularism was inherent in the constitutional scheme and forms part of the basic structure.

s: Part XIV-A, added by the 42nd Amendment, deals with which of the following?
x: The 42nd Amendment added Part XIV-A on tribunals, listed Fundamental Duties in Article 51A and shifted education to the Concurrent List.

s: Which change made by the 42nd Amendment was later undone?
o: Six-year term of the Lok Sabha
x: The 44th Amendment restored the five-year term; the Preamble words and Fundamental Duties remain.

s: Which Directive Principles were newly inserted by the 42nd Amendment?
x: The 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A and 43A (also 39(f) and 48A) to the DPSPs.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers binding on the President?
x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 made ministerial advice binding on the President.

s: Why is the 42nd Amendment, 1976 called the 'Mini-Constitution'?
o: It changed the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule and 54 Articles
It replaced the whole Constitution of 1950
It was ratified by all the States
x: It is called the Mini-Constitution because it changed the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule and 54 Articles.

s: The 42nd Amendment froze the allocation of seats for delimitation on the basis of which Census?
x: The 42nd Amendment froze delimitation on the 1971 Census; the 84th later extended the freeze to 2026.

s: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988, brought about which of the following changes?
o: Reduction of the voting age from 21 years to 18 years
Introduction of Electors' Photo Identity Cards
Linking of electoral rolls with Aadhaar
x: The 61st Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years; the change came into force in 1989.

s: On which date did the 61st Amendment, which lowered the voting age to 18, come into force?
x: The 61st Amendment came into force on 28 March 1989 and was first used in the 1989 general election.

s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the 73rd Amendment?
x: Constitutional status to Municipalities came with the 74th Amendment; the other three belong to the 73rd.

s: The 12th Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment, contains how many subjects?
x: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IX-A and the 12th Schedule with 18 subjects; the 11th Schedule of the 73rd has 29.

s: Part IXA relating to municipalities was added by which Amendment?
x: Part IXA on municipalities came with the 74th Amendment; the 73rd added Part IX (Panchayats) and the Eleventh Schedule.

s: On which date did the 73rd Constitutional Amendment on Panchayats come into force?
x: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993; the 74th came into force on 1 June 1993.

s: On which date did the 74th Constitutional Amendment on Municipalities come into force?
x: The 74th Amendment (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule) came into force on 1 June 1993.

s: By which Amendment were Articles 239AA and 239AB, on Delhi's special status, inserted?
x: The 69th Amendment gave Delhi its framework; the 52nd introduced the Tenth Schedule and the 86th inserted Article 21A.

s: Which Amendment barred defectors from becoming Ministers?
x: The 91st Amendment (2003) barred defectors from becoming Ministers; the 52nd (1985) had introduced anti-defection disqualification.

s: What did the earlier Tenth Schedule, added by the 35th Amendment, 1974, deal with?
x: The 35th Amendment (1974) added a Tenth Schedule on Sikkim's associate status; the anti-defection Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment (1985).

s: What did the 89th Amendment, 2003 provide for?
o: Separate NCSC and NCST under Articles 338 and 338A
Ministers limited to 15% of the House
x: The 89th split the commission into the NCSC and NCST (338, 338A); the 15% limit was the 91st and Delhi NCT the 69th.

s: What did the 62nd Constitutional Amendment, 1989 provide for?
o: Extension of SC/ST seat reservation in legislatures to 2000
Lowering of the voting age to 18
x: The 62nd Amendment extended SC/ST seat reservation in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies up to 2000; anti-defection was the 52nd.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The 52nd Amendment added the Tenth Schedule. The 1st added the Ninth, the 73rd the Eleventh and the 74th the Twelfth Schedule.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment substituted the word 'amount' for 'compensation' in Article 31 and inserted Article 31C?
x: The 25th Amendment (1971), after the Bank Nationalisation case, replaced 'compensation' with 'amount' in Article 31 and inserted Article 31C. The 24th (1971) dealt with Parliament's power to amend FRs and Art. 13(4); the 42nd widened Art. 31C; the 44th removed property from Part III.

s: By which Amendment were privy purses abolished?
x: The 26th abolished privy purses; the 24th made presidential assent compulsory, the 44th removed property from FRs and the 52nd added anti-defection law.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Amendment)
A. 12th Amendment
B. 15th Amendment
C. 58th Amendment
D. 96th Amendment
List-II (Change)
1. Authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution
2. 'Oriya' changed to 'Odia'
3. Goa, Daman and Diu made a Union Territory
4. Retirement age of High Court judges raised from 60 to 62
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: 12th (1962) made Goa, Daman and Diu a UT; 15th (1963) raised HC judges' retirement age to 62; 58th (1987) gave the Hindi text; 96th (2011) changed Oriya to Odia.

s: Which one of the following was a major feature of the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956?
o: Creation of the National Capital Territory of Delhi
Reorganisation of States and abolition of the former Part A, Part B, Part C and Part D classification
x: The Seventh Amendment, 1956 accompanied the reorganisation of States, abolished the Part A, B, C and D classification, repealed Part VII and dealt with Union Territories.

s: Which Amendment raised the retirement age of High Court judges from 60 to 62?
x: The 15th Amendment (1963) raised the HC judges' retirement age from 60 to 62; the 12th (1962) made Goa, Daman and Diu a Union Territory.

s: Up to which year did the 84th Amendment extend the freeze of seat allocation on the 1971 Census?
x: The 84th Amendment froze seat allocation on the 1971 Census until 2026, not 2030.

s: The delimitation freeze was extended up to 2026 by which Amendment?
x: The 84th Amendment extended the freeze to 2026; the issue is now linked to the 2027 Census, and the 131st Bill failed in April 2026.

s: Reservation in promotions for SCs and STs under Article 16(4A) was introduced by which Amendment?
x: The 77th Amendment (1995) inserted Article 16(4A) for reservation in promotions.

s: 'Consequential seniority' for SCs/STs in promotions was provided by which Amendment?
x: The 85th Amendment (2001) added consequential seniority to 16(4A), retrospective from 17 June 1995.

s: The 82nd Amendment allowed relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion through a proviso to which Article?
x: The 82nd Amendment (2000) added a proviso to Article 335; Article 16(4B) was the 81st.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 81st Amendment – carry forward of unfilled vacancies outside the 50% ceiling
x: The 81st inserted 16(4B) on carry-forward vacancies; consequential seniority was the 85th, 16(4A) the 77th, and the 62nd extended SC/ST seats.

s: The 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Amendments were all upheld in which case?
x: All four SC/ST reservation amendments were upheld in M. Nagaraj (2006).

s: Which Constitutional Amendment restored the five-year term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies after the Forty-second Amendment had extended it to six years?
x: The Forty-fourth Amendment, 1978 restored the normal five-year term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies and restored judicial review in important respects.

s: Which Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' as a ground for National Emergency?
x: The 44th Amendment made this change and also let the President return ministerial advice once.

s: Who can disapprove or revoke a Proclamation of Emergency under the safeguard associated with the Forty-fourth Amendment?
x: The Forty-fourth Amendment strengthened the power of the Lok Sabha to disapprove or revoke a Proclamation of Emergency.

s: After the 44th Amendment, under which Article is the right to property a legal right?
x: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and kept property as a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

s: The Forty-fourth Amendment restored the power of courts to hear election disputes relating to which set of offices?
o: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker of the Lok Sabha
President, Governor, Prime Minister and Chief Justice of India
Vice-President, Chief Minister, Speaker and Attorney-General
President, Vice-President, Governors and Chief Ministers
x: It reversed the bar created by the Thirty-ninth Amendment and restored judicial consideration of election disputes concerning the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Speaker.

s: After the 44th Amendment, rights under which Articles cannot be suspended during a National Emergency?
x: The 44th Amendment provides that Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.

s: The 44th Amendment was enacted by the Janata government of which Prime Minister?
x: The Janata government under PM Morarji Desai enacted the 44th Amendment as a corrective to the 38th, 39th and 42nd.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 44th Amendment, 1978:
1. A National Emergency can be proclaimed only on the written recommendation of the Cabinet.
2. The President may return the advice of the Council of Ministers once for reconsideration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 44th Amendment required written Cabinet advice for an Emergency and allowed the President to return ministerial advice once.

s: Under the 44th Amendment, how many times may the President return the advice of the Council of Ministers for reconsideration?
x: The 44th Amendment lets the President return ministerial advice once; he must act on the advice given after reconsideration.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the rulings overcome by the First Amendment?
o: Kameshwar Singh v. State of Bihar concerned zamindari abolition / land reform
Articles 31A and 31B were the direct response to Champakam Dorairajan
Romesh Thappar (1950) concerned freedom of speech
Champakam Dorairajan concerned a communal order in admissions, leading to Article 15(4)
x: Champakam Dorairajan led to Article 15(4); Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule answered the land-reform judgments.

s: On which date did President Rajendra Prasad give assent to the First Amendment?
x: The First Amendment, enacted by the Provisional Parliament under PM Nehru, received assent on 18 June 1951.

s: Which provision added by the First Amendment, 1951 validates Acts placed in the Ninth Schedule?
x: Article 31B validates Ninth Schedule Acts; Article 31A saves estate-acquisition laws and Article 15(4) permits special provisions for backward classes, SCs and STs.

s: The constitutional validity of the First Amendment was upheld in which case?
x: The First Amendment was upheld by the Supreme Court in Shankari Prasad (1951).

s: Who was the Prime Minister when the First Constitutional Amendment, 1951 was enacted?
x: The First Amendment was enacted in 1951 under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

s: Which body enacted the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951?
o: A joint sitting of both Houses
x: The First Amendment was enacted by the Provisional Parliament, before the first Lok Sabha was elected.

s: Which of the following was NOT a provision associated with the First Constitutional Amendment?
o: Reservation of one-third seats for women in State Assemblies
x: Reservation of one-third seats for women in State Assemblies is associated with the 106th Amendment, not the First Amendment. The First Amendment dealt with Article 15(4), Article 19(2), and the Ninth Schedule.

s: Goa became a State of India under which Constitutional Amendment?
x: The Fifty-sixth Amendment of 1987 dealt with Goa’s statehood and inserted Article 371I.

s: Which Amendment made Sikkim a full State?
x: The 36th (1975) made Sikkim a full State; the 13th (1962) dealt with Nagaland and the 55th (1986) gave Arunachal Pradesh statehood.

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
x: The Fifty-third Amendment of 1986 dealt with Mizoram statehood. The Fifty-fifth concerned Arunachal Pradesh and the Fifty-sixth concerned Goa.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The 89th Amendment bifurcated the National Commission for SCs/STs into the NCSC and NCST.
The 83rd Amendment exempted Arunachal Pradesh from reservations for Scheduled Castes in Panchayats.
The 13th Amendment added Article 371A for special provisions relating to Arunachal Pradesh.
The 105th Amendment restored the power of State Governments and UTs to identify and notify their own SEBCs.
x: Option C is incorrect: the 13th Amendment's Article 371A is for Nagaland, not Arunachal Pradesh. The 89th split the SC/ST Commission, the 83rd exempted Arunachal from SC Panchayat quotas, and the 105th restored States' power to list SEBCs.

s: Nagaland became a State through which Amendment, which also inserted Article 371A?
x: The 13th Amendment (1962) made Nagaland a State with Article 371A.

s: Arunachal Pradesh became a State with Article 371H through which Amendment?
x: The 55th Amendment (1986) is Arunachal Pradesh; the 53rd is Mizoram and the 56th Goa.

s: The constitutional provisions relating to the Six-Point Formula and the Central University in Andhra Pradesh (Articles 371D and 371E) were inserted by which amendment?
x: The 32nd Amendment Act, 1973 inserted Article 371D (the AP Six-Point Formula on public employment and education) and Article 371E (a Central University in Andhra Pradesh). It was the 32nd, not the 33rd.

s: What does Article 371E, inserted by the 32nd Amendment, provide for?
o: A Central University in Andhra Pradesh
x: Article 371E provides for a Central University in AP; the Six-Point Formula is Article 371D.

s: By which of the following were Articles 371D and 371E extended to Telangana?
x: The AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 extended Articles 371D and 371E to Telangana.

s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sequence of the First, Forty-second, Fifty-second, Eighty-sixth and Ninety-sixth Amendments with their years?
x: The years are 1951, 1976, 1985, 2002 and 2011 respectively.

s: Article 15(5), enabling OBC reservation in educational institutions, was inserted by which Amendment?
x: The 93rd Amendment (2005) added Article 15(5); the 86th (2002) added Article 21A.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: 86th Amendment – Right to Education for children aged 6–14
91st Amendment – 15% cap on the Council of Ministers
x: The 106th Amendment provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; EWS reservation came with the 103rd.

s: The Ninety-sixth Constitutional Amendment changed the name ‘Oriya’ to which name?
x: The Ninety-sixth Amendment, enacted in 2011, changed the constitutional reference from ‘Oriya’ to ‘Odia’.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: 97th Amendment (2011) – Part IX-B, permitting a maximum of 31 directors under Article 243ZJ
91st Amendment (2003) – Barred defectors from ministerial posts (Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A))
101st Amendment (2016) – GST and the GST Council under Article 279A
x: Article 243ZJ, added by the 97th Amendment, permits a maximum of 21 directors, not 31.

s: Under Article 243ZJ, what is the maximum number of directors on a co-operative board?
x: The 97th Amendment's Article 243ZJ caps the board at 21 directors, not 31.

s: What is the term of the board of a co-operative society under the constitutional provisions?
x: The board has a five-year term; the provisions also fix a maximum of 21 directors, one SC/ST seat, two women seats and audit within six months.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court strike down Part IXB insofar as it applied to State co-operative societies?
o: Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah (2021)
x: In Rajendra N. Shah (2021), Part IXB (Articles 243ZH–243ZT, added by the 97th Amendment) was struck down for State co-operatives as State ratification was absent.

s: Which Article was inserted into the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 97th Constitutional Amendment?
x: Article 43B was inserted to promote the voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control and professional management of co-operative societies.

s: In Rajendra N. Shah v. Union of India (2021), why was Part IXB held inapplicable to State co-operative societies?
o: It dealt exclusively with municipal bodies
It had been repealed by the 105th Amendment
It had not been ratified by the States as required
x: The Supreme Court struck down Part IXB in its application to State co-operative societies because the required ratification by the States had not been obtained. It continues to operate for multi-State co-operative societies.

s: Under the 97th Amendment, for whom must a co-operative board reserve seats?
o: Two SC/ST members and one woman
One SC/ST member and two women
x: Co-operative boards reserve one seat for SC/ST and two for women, with a 5-year term.

s: Which Article was amended by the 97th Amendment to make the right to form co-operative societies a Fundamental Right?
x: The 97th Amendment (2011) added co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(c); Article 43B is the Directive Principle it added.

s:
Consider the following statements about Part IXB (co-operative societies):
1. A co-operative board can have a maximum of 21 directors.
2. The accounts must be audited within six months of the close of the financial year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: Article 243ZJ caps the board at 21 directors, and audit must be done within six months of the end of the financial year.

s: Which Article inserted by the 101st Amendment created the GST Council?
x: Article 279A created the GST Council; 246A gives concurrent GST power and 269A covers inter-State supply.

s: Which Article was omitted by the 101st Amendment?
x: The 101st omitted Article 268A (service tax) and inserted 246A, 269A and 279A.

s: What does Article 246A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, provide for?
o: Power of both Parliament and States to make GST laws
x: 246A lets Parliament and the States both make GST laws; 269A is inter-State supply and 279A the GST Council.

s: By what majority does the GST Council take its decisions?
x: The GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, decides by a three-fourths majority.

s: From which date was the Goods and Services Tax, introduced by the 101st Amendment, rolled out?
x: The 101st Amendment got assent on 8 September 2016 and GST came into effect from 1 July 2017.

s: Who chairs the GST Council under Article 279A?
o: The Chairman of the Finance Commission
x: The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and decides by a three-fourths majority.

s: Which Article, inserted by the 102nd Amendment, gave constitutional status to the NCBC?
x: Article 338B made the NCBC constitutional; 342A lets the President notify the SEBC list.

s: Through which Article did the 105th Amendment restore the States' power to identify their own SEBCs?
x: The 105th inserted 342A(3), letting States/UTs identify their own SEBCs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 102nd and 105th Amendments:
1. The 102nd Amendment received assent on 11 August 2018.
2. The 105th Amendment took away the States' power to identify SEBCs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 105th restored the States' power to identify SEBCs.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes?
x: The 102nd Amendment, 2018 inserted Article 338B and made the NCBC a constitutional body.

s: Which Article inserted by the 106th Amendment reserves seats for women in State Legislative Assemblies?
x: Article 332A covers State Assemblies; 330A covers the Lok Sabha and 334A the timing.

s: For how many years does women's reservation under the 106th Amendment last, unless extended by Parliament?
x: It lasts 15 years from commencement, extendable by Parliament by law.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 106th Amendment (women's reservation):
1. The reservation starts only after delimitation based on the first Census taken after its commencement.
2. The reservation lasts 15 years and cannot be extended by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The quota begins only after delimitation on the first Census after commencement. It lasts 15 years but Parliament can extend it by law, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: To the completion of which of the following has the implementation of women's reservation under the 2023 law been linked?
x: The women's reservation remains unimplemented because its implementation is linked to the completion of delimitation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 106th Constitutional Amendment?
o: It has been criticised for not providing a separate sub-quota for BC women
Southern States fear their share may decline after delimitation
It has already been implemented in all State Legislative Assemblies
It provides one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
x: The women's quota under the 106th Amendment remains unimplemented.

s: Under which Articles has one-third reservation for women in Panchayats and Municipalities been provided since 1992?
x: Articles 243D and 243T deal with reservation in Panchayats and Municipalities respectively, giving women one-third seats since 1992.

s: In which year did the 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) receive Presidential assent?
x: It received assent on 28 September 2023.

s: Under which Article are seats reserved for women in the Lok Sabha by the 106th Amendment?
x: Article 330A covers the Lok Sabha; 332A State Assemblies; 243T is municipal women's reservation.

s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was created by which Amendment?
x: The 99th Amendment (2014) created the NJAC, which the Supreme Court struck down in 2015 for violating judicial independence.

s: In which year did the Supreme Court strike down the 99th Amendment, which created the National Judicial Appointments Commission?
x: The 99th Amendment (2014) creating the NJAC was struck down in 2015 to protect judicial independence.

s: The National Judicial Appointments Commission was provided for by which Amendment?
x: The 99th Amendment, 2014 provided for the NJAC, struck down in 2015; the 97th, 100th and 102nd dealt with co-operatives, the Land Boundary Agreement and the NCBC.

s: Which of the following is the latest enacted Constitutional Amendment Act?
x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 2023, is the latest enacted amendment in the sequence. The 105th Amendment of 2021 is therefore not the latest.

s: The 100th Amendment implemented the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement covering how many Indian enclaves?
x: The 100th Amendment (2015) covered 111 Indian and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves.

s: Which recent Constitutional Amendment is the only one struck down as a whole by the Supreme Court?
x: The 99th Amendment (NJAC) was struck down as a whole; the 97th was struck down only in part (Rajendra N. Shah).

s: With which of the following is the 104th Amendment associated?
x: The 104th ended Anglo-Indian nominations; EWS came with the 103rd, GST with the 101st and women's reservation with the 106th.

s: The 103rd Amendment was passed as which Constitution Amendment Bill?
x: The EWS amendment was passed as the 124th Amendment Bill, 2019.

s: By what majority did the Supreme Court uphold the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan (2022)?
x: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (7 Nov 2022) upheld the EWS amendment by 3:2.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment extended the reservation of seats under Article 334 up to 2030 and also ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians to legislatures?
x: The 104th Constitutional Amendment, 2019, extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs up to 2030 and ended Anglo-Indian nomination.

s: Which clauses did the 103rd Amendment insert for EWS reservation?
x: The 103rd inserted 15(6) for education and 16(6) for jobs, up to 10% for EWS.

s: On which date did the 103rd Amendment receive Presidential assent?
x: The 103rd received assent on 12 January 2019; 7 November 2022 is the Janhit Abhiyan judgment.

s:
Consider the following statements about Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022):
1. It upheld the 103rd Amendment by a 3:2 majority.
2. It held that the 50% ceiling applies to EWS reservation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 50% ceiling applies to 15(4), 15(5) and 16(4), not EWS.

s: Under the 103rd Amendment, up to what household income limit is a family treated as Economically Weaker Section (EWS) for reservation?
x: The 10% EWS quota under Articles 15(6) and 16(6) covers households with income up to Rs 8 lakh.

s: From which month and year did the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and Assemblies end?
x: The 104th Amendment ended Anglo-Indian nomination, effective January 2020.

s: Up to which year did the 104th Amendment extend SC/ST seat reservation under Article 334?
x: The 104th extended SC/ST seat reservation in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies to 2030.

s: Which of the following Articles is proposed to be inserted by the 129th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2024?
x: The 129th Amendment Bill proposes insertion of Article 82A and amendments to Articles 83, 172 and 327 in connection with simultaneous elections.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 2025?
o: It concerns removal of the PM, CMs and Ministers detained for 30 consecutive days on serious charges
It increases the Lok Sabha strength to 850 members
x: Raising the Lok Sabha to 850 was the 131st Bill; the 130th concerns removal of Ministers detained for 30 consecutive days and amends Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.

s: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024 on One Nation, One Election inserts Article 82A. Which Articles does it amend?
x: The 129th Bill amends Articles 83, 172 and 327; 75, 164 and 239AA belong to the 130th Bill.

s: Who chairs the Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 on One Nation, One Election?
x: The 129th Amendment Bill on simultaneous elections is with a JPC chaired by P.P. Chaudhary.
